provenance.gatheredBy: load-sport-data, the 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup semifinals and final as played: the semifinals on 15 August at Eden Park, Auckland (Spain beat Sweden 2-1) and 16 August at Stadium Australia, Sydney (England beat Australia 3-1), and the final at Stadium Australia on 20 August (Spain beat England 1-0). Each event is one game for each team. The field is every outfield player in either side's matchday squad (goalkeepers left out), her position (defender, midfielder or forward) from FIFA's match centre where she started a match of the round and otherwise from ESPN's athlete record, and her country the side's (England as GB); a player who came on or started has a line, an unused substitute none. Each line's shots on target are ESPN's; goals and assists are ESPN's too, cross-checked against FIFA's match timelines, which agree on every one. Ranking is the player's Hat Trick total at the 2023 tournament before the round (3 per goal + 2 per assist + shots on target), from ESPN's tournament statistics less the round's matches (for the semifinals, less the final too); ties go by name.
